question:
Figure 1 is the golden sample (a known-good reference part) and figure 2 is the part currently under test. The two frames were shot on the same fixture and are pixel-aligned, but their exposure differs slightly. The candidate regions below are normalized [x1, y1, x2, y2] in [0, 1] (origin top-left). At most one region of figure 2 contains a manufacturing defect that the golden sample does not have. Which region contains the defect?
(A) [0.3314, 0.5170, 0.4514, 0.6370]
(B) [0.2120, 0.2100, 0.3320, 0.3300]
(C) [0.7931, 0.3005, 0.9131, 0.4205]
(D) No defect in any of the above regions.

Answer with only the correct option letter.

First, I'll draw a coordinate grid over [img2] to help visualize the regions more clearly.

<tool_call>
{"name": "draw_normalized_coordinate_grid", "arguments": {"grid_rows": 4, "grid_cols": 4, "target_image": "[img2]"}}
</tool_call>

Now that I have the grid overlay on [img2], I can see that there is a small, distinct feature (possibly a defect) in the second row and first column (i.e., the region around [0.25, 0.25] to [0.50, 0.50]). This corresponds to region (B) which is [0.2120, 0.2100, 0.3320, 0.3300].

To confirm, I'll now crop [img2] to isolate region (B) and compare it with the corresponding region in [img1].

<tool_call>
{"name": "crop", "arguments": {"x1": 0.2120, "y1": 0.2100, "x2": 0.3320, "y2": 0.3300, "target_image": "[img2]"}}
</tool_call>

After cropping region (B) from [img2], I can see a small, irregularly shaped defect in [img4] that does not appear in the corresponding region of [img1]. The defect appears as a slight discoloration or a small hole with a bright edge, which is not present in the golden sample.

To be sure, I'll now crop the same region from [img1] to compare directly.

<tool_call>
{"name": "crop", "arguments": {"x1": 0.2120, "y1": 0.2100, "x2": 0.3320, "y2": 0.3300, "target_image": "[img1]"}}
</tool_call>

After cropping the same region (B) from [img1], I can see that this region in the golden sample is uniform and shows no defects. The texture is consistent with the rest of [img1]. In contrast, [img4] shows a clear defect.

To further confirm, I'll now compare [img4] and [img5] side by side.

<tool_call>
{"name": "make_collage", "arguments": {"rows": 2, "cols": 2, "target_images": ["[img4]", "[img5]"]}}
</tool_call>

After comparing [img4] and [img5] side by side in [img6], it is clear that [img4] shows a defect (a small, irregularly shaped feature with a bright edge) that is not present in [img5]. The region in [img1] (shown in [img5]) is uniform and free of defects.

Therefore, the correct answer is (B).

<answer> B </answer>
